title: Developer Experience Docs: Ops, SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Support Playbook
author: Ava Chen
body:
# Developer Experience Docs: Ops, SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Support Playbook

Summary
This page documents the developer experience (DevEx) documentation operating procedures and canonical content set we maintain for Redwood Inference: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. The goal is to ensure consistent, discoverable, and testable docs that minimize support load and accelerate developer onboarding.

Goals
- Provide consistent, high-quality SDK guides (Python, JS, Java) with runnable examples.
- Ship and maintain a small set of curated quickstarts for common production patterns.
- Keep API examples canonical, tested, and versioned alongside SDK releases.
- Operate the docs site (redwood-docs-site) with predictable publishing, CI, and alerting.
- Maintain a short list of top support issues with reproducible fixes to reduce triage time.

Scope
This page covers: documentation authoring standards, the docs CI/publishing workflow, SDK guide templates, quickstart catalog and templates, canonical API examples, and the top 10 support issues with reproduction and fixes. It does not replace team-specific runbooks for product or infra changes (see related pages).

---

## 1. Docs site operating procedures

Owner: eng-developer-experience (primary), eng-platform (infra support)
Service: redwood-docs-site (Hugo + static assets, deployed via docs-deploy-bot)

SLOs and key metrics
- Publishing success rate: 99.5% (measured per CI run)
- Time from merge to live: median < 15 minutes for docs-only changes
- Search indexing lag: <= 10 minutes after deploy
- Search query 99th percentile latency: < 300ms

CI / Publishing workflow (standard)
1. Author creates a docs branch from main and opens a PR against docs/main.
2. PR must reference applicable docs template (see Templates section) and include 'docs-changelog' entry when content affects behavior.
3. Automated checks (docs-lint, spellcheck, linkcheck, sample-snippet-runner) run in docs CI.
4. At least one reviewer from eng-developer-experience approves the PR.
5. Merge triggers docs CI build. If build passes, docs-deploy-bot performs staged deploy to staging.
6. Staging smoke tests run (search, homepage, 3 canonical quickstarts). On success, deploy to production is scheduled within 10 minutes.

Emergency publish / rollback
- Emergency publish: tag PR with 'emergency-publish' and notify #docs-ops; a release engineer will perform a force deploy after a quick approval from an oncall docs owner.
- Rollback: docs-deploy-bot supports quick rollback to last successful build. To rollback, run: 
```
# rollback to previous build
./scripts/docs-deploy rollback --service redwood-docs-site --env prod
```

Backups and retention
- All markdown content is stored in Git (source of truth). Static site snapshots are kept for 90 days in the S3 docs-snapshots bucket.

Indexing and search maintenance
- Search index built by docs-indexer job on deploy. If indexer fails, open incident and run manual indexer via: `./scripts/docs-index rebuild --force`
- Reindex schedule for major releases: run a full reindex during low-traffic window (Sun 02:00 UTC).

Monitoring and alerts (alerts in #docs-alerts Slack)
- Deploy failure: P1 if >1 failed deploy in 30 minutes.
- Search errors: P2 if error rate > 0.5% over 5m.
- Publishing latency breach: P3 if median > 30 minutes for >30 minutes.

Ownership matrix
| Area | Primary | Secondary | Oncall |
|---|---|---|---|
| Docs content & review | eng-developer-experience | developer-advocacy | oncall-docs |
| CI & deploy | eng-platform | eng-devex | infra-oncall |
| Search & index | eng-platform | eng-developer-experience | infra-oncall |

---

## 2. SDK guides (authoring standards and template)

Purpose: SDK guides provide idiomatic examples, installation instructions, and migration notes for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Java SDKs. Each SDK guide must be runnable and include pinned example versions.

Required sections for every SDK guide (use the SDK doc template):
- Title and short summary (1\u20132 lines)
- Supported versions & compatibility table
- Installation (pip/npm/maven coordinates)
- Initialization and auth (examples using API key + env var pattern)
- Quick example (single-file run)
- Common patterns (streaming, function/tool calling, embeddings)
- Error handling & retries (with recommended backoff policy)
- Migration notes (breaking changes, deprecations)
- Tests & snippet-runner cases (link to CI job)

SDK guide template (example snippet)
```
# Quickstart: Python SDK
pip install redwood-sdk
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=\"<key>\"

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
print(client.generate("Hello from Redwood"))
```

Snippet testing
- All SDK code snippets must be included in `docs/snippets/<sdk>/` and wired to the `snippet-runner` CI job. The job runs snippets in isolated environments (venv, node containers) and reports failures as PR checks.

Versioned docs and compatibility
- SDK docs are versioned in docs site with path prefixes: `/sdk/python/vX.Y/`. Each release must include compatibility notes for models supported and recommended runtime settings.

---

## 3. Quickstarts & templates (catalog and usage)

Purpose: Provide end-to-end examples that let engineers go from zero to deployed app in ~10\u201330 minutes. Quickstarts are opinionated and ready-to-run. Templates are smaller building blocks (auth pattern, prompt engineering pattern, streaming handler).

Quickstart catalog (top items)
| Quickstart | Description | Owner | Path |
|---|---|---|---|
| embeddings-search | Small app: index docs with embeddings and run k-NN search | eng-developer-experience | /quickstarts/embeddings-search |
| chat-productivity | Chat UI with function-calling and user message routing | developer-advocacy | /quickstarts/chat-productivity |
| reranker-pipeline | Use embeddings + reranker to improve recall/precision | applied-ml | /quickstarts/reranker-pipeline |
| streaming-chat | Low-latency streaming chat sample (websocket + SSE) | eng-developer-experience | /quickstarts/streaming-chat |

Template catalog (examples)
- prompt-template: reusable prompt engineering helper (owner: applied-ml)
- auth-env: env-var based auth + local testing script (owner: eng-developer-experience)
- infra-terraform: terraform module for deploying Redwood Dedicated test environment (owner: eng-infra)

How to add a new quickstart
1. Create a new repo under `redwood/quickstarts/<name>` and add a docs quickstart page referencing it.
2. Include a Dockerfile and a small e2e test (max 3 steps) that can run in CI.
3. Add the quickstart to the quickstarts table in the docs PR.
4. CI runs smoke test: build image, run container, exercise health endpoint.

Quickstart template example (init script)
```
# create a new quickstart scaffold
./scripts/quickstart init --name my-quickstart --template embeddings-search
```

---

## 4. Canonical API examples

Principles
- Keep examples minimal, idiomatic, and tested.
- Provide both REST and SDK examples for each workflow.
- Mark examples that are production-ready vs example-only.

Canonical examples to include in docs (must be runnable via snippet-runner)
1. Text generation (sync + streaming) — REST + Python/JS SDK.
2. Chat with function/tool calling — SDK-first example and policy for tool schemas.
3. Embeddings indexing + search — REST bulk endpoint + SDK.
4. Reranking workflow — combine generation + embeddings.

Example: Python text generation (SDK)
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = client.generate("Write a short haiku about low-latency inference.")
print(resp.text)
```

Example: REST curl (streaming)
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-1.1 \
  -d '{\"prompt\":\"Tell me a joke\"}'
```

Versioning and deprecation policy for examples
- Examples are tagged with SDK and API versions. When an API change is required, mark examples with `deprecation-date` and add migration examples.

---

## 5. Top support issues & canonical fixes (triage playbook)

This section lists the top recurring support problems reported by SDK users and the canonical resolution. Use this as the first-source during Tier 1 triage. Keep the list short and actionable.

Issue 1: Authentication errors (401 / missing API key)\- Symptom: SDK calls return 401 or 403 with message "missing or invalid API key".\- Likely root cause: API key not set in env var, expired key, or key scoped to different account.\- Reproduction: Run `python examples/gen.py` without REDWOOD_API_KEY set.\- Canonical fix: Ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is exported, verify key in Console -> API keys, rotate key if expired. Provide this snippet: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_...`\- Owner: customer-success / eng-developer-experience

Issue 2: Streaming responses hang or time out\- Symptom: SDK or curl stream hangs after first chunk.\- Likely root cause: Proxy or corporate firewall terminating SSE/HTTP2 long-lived connections; incorrect Accept header.\- Canonical fix: Validate connection with `curl -N` and set `Accept: text/event-stream`. Recommend switching to websockets-based sample for restricted networks.

Issue 3: High token cost from naive prompting\- Symptom: Unexpectedly high per-request token usage.\- Root cause: Unbounded system prompt or not truncating long context.\- Canonical fix: Use prompt templates, limit history length, and enable prefix caching. Provide sample patch to use `client.generate(..., max_tokens=256)` and guidance to use embeddings + retrieval for long contexts.

Issue 4: SDK snippet tests failing in CI for new PRs\- Symptom: snippet-runner job fails on new docs PR.\- Root cause: Missing dependency or breaking API in upstream SDK release.\- Canonical fix: Repro locally with `./scripts/snippet-runner run --sdk python` and update snippets or pin dependency; coordinate with SDK owners.

Issue 5: Quickstart fails health check in CI\- Symptom: quickstart e2e fails on health endpoint.\- Root cause: Environment variable not configured or container startup args changed.\- Canonical fix: Check container logs (`docker logs`) and ensure CI provides required envs. Update quickstart README with explicit env matrix.

Issue 6: Search returns outdated results after docs update\- Symptom: New doc content not searchable.\- Root cause: Indexer failed or deploy step skipped indexing.\- Canonical fix: Trigger manual reindex `./scripts/docs-index rebuild --force` and check docs-indexer logs in CloudWatch.

Issue 7: Inconsistent model naming between API examples and SDKs\- Symptom: Examples refer to `redwood-1` while SDK expects `redwood-1.1`.\- Canonical fix: Use canonical model alias variable in examples ({{MODEL_ALIAS}}) and update snippet-runner to substitute the recommended alias mapped in `docs/config/models.yaml`.

Issue 8: Local dev vs production environment mismatch\- Symptom: Quickstarts work locally but fail in staging/prod.\- Canonical fix: Provide `env.example` and `docker-compose.ci.yml` for parity. Document common differences (CORS, callback URLs, auth scopes).

Triage steps (quick)
1. Reproduce locally using the same SDK version and sample.
2. Check API key and permissions.
3. Run snippet-runner for the relevant SDK.
4. If a docs issue, open a docs PR with failing snippet and tag `docs-fix`.
5. If infra-related, escalate to eng-platform via #infra-help with replication steps.

---

## 6. Release notes & documentation lifecycle
- Docs changes that are purely editorial: no changelog entry required.
- Docs changes that affect user behavior or APIs: add a `docs-changelog` entry and notify `#product-updates`.
- Monthly docs audit: eng-developer-experience reviews top 20 pages for accuracy and snippet health.

---

## Appendix: Useful commands and snippets
- Run snippet tests locally: `./scripts/snippet-runner run --all`
- Build docs locally: `./scripts/docs-build --watch`
- Deploy to staging (release engineer): `./scripts/docs-deploy promote --build 12345 --env staging`
- Reindex search: `./scripts/docs-index rebuild --force`
